div.div:
Hop 1 client to gateway
AI Security → AI Gateway → Security Keys
Two tabs, Service and User. The tab decides attribution, and
it decides which upstream auth types will work.
The key must carry the mcp.invoke permission.
Hop 2 gateway to MCP server
AI Security → AI Gateway → Integrations → MCP Registry
The Authentication control on the registry entry: OAuth 2.1,
OAuth Client Credentials, None, or Headers.
Neither hop knows about the other. A correct registry entry still
fails if the client presents the wrong kind of key, and a correct key
still fails if the registry entry points at the wrong URL.

div.div:
OAuth 2.1 on a registry entry is per user. Each person signs in to the
upstream service themselves, so the request must arrive carrying a user
identity. A Service key is tied to nobody, so there is no one to sign in.
Upstream auth type Service key User key
None yes yes
Headers yes yes
OAuth Client Credentials yes yes
OAuth 2.1 (per user) no yes
The key type is fixed when the key is created and cannot be converted, so
this decision comes before the registry entry rather than after it. The
symptom is a 500 reading Unable to verify user access, which reads
like a permissions fault rather than a wrong kind of credential.

text.tspan: OAuth 2.1 on a registry entry is per user. Each person signs in to the
upstream service themselves, so the request must arrive carrying a user
identity. A Service key is tied to nobody, so there is no one to sign in.
Upstream auth type Service key User key
None yes yes
Headers yes yes
OAuth Client Credentials yes yes
OAuth 2.1 (per user) no yes
The key type is fixed when the key is created and cannot be converted, so
this decision comes before the registry entry rather than after it. The
symptom is a 500 reading Unable to verify user access, which reads
like a permissions fault rather than a wrong kind of credential.

div.b: What the log holds, and what it does not

switch.text: What the log holds, and what it does not

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 716px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#333333, #c1c1c1); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Every request is logged with no setup. Each entry carries the tool, the full
parameters, the full response, the user, the team, a timestamp, the latency,
the status, and which server answered.
Tool arguments are logged in full. A tool that takes a customer record or a
query string puts that value in the log. Whether capture can be redacted for
a sensitive tool is not documented.
Attribution comes from the key the request arrived on. A User key names the
person. A Service key names the workspace and nothing finer, so every
application sharing that key is indistinguishable in the log.

text.tspan: Every request is logged with no setup. Each entry carries the tool, the full
parameters, the full response, the user, the team, a timestamp, the latency,
the status, and which server answered.
Tool arguments are logged in full. A tool that takes a customer record or a
query string puts that value in the log. Whether capture can be redacted for
a sensitive tool is not documented.
Attribution comes from the key the request arrived on. A User key names the
person. A Service key names the workspace and nothing finer, so every
application sharing that key is indistinguishable in the log.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 716px; margin-left: 751px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;

div.div:
A client usually reports one generic error, so the message describes the hop
that did not fail. Check hop 2 first.
401 Missing or expired token, or the server wants a sign-in.
403 Authenticated but not allowed. Wrong workspace or server in the
URL, or no access to that server.
404 Wrong slug, or the server is not registered in this workspace.
500 Unable to verify user access. Start at the key type.
The slug in the URL is the registry slug, never a UUID. Copy the connection
URL from the server's own page rather than assembling it by hand.

404 Wrong slug, or the server is not registered in this workspace.
500 Unable to verify user access. Start at the key type.
The slug in the URL is the registry slug, never a UUID. Copy the connection
URL from the server's own page rather than assembling it by hand.
